chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the servant stands in prayer and lightens his prayer, Allah, Blessed and High, says to His angels: 'Do you not look at My servant? It is as if he sees that the fulfillment of his needs is in the hand of someone other than Me. Does he not know that the fulfillment of his needs is in My Hand?'

key_terms.بِيَدِ غَيْرِي: In the hand of someone other than Me
key_terms.فَخَفَّفَ صَلَاتَهُ: He lightened/shortened his prayer (rushed through it)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean when a servant 'lightens' their prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) critiques 'hurried prayer' (khuff al-salat) not merely as a ritual error, but as a spiritual symptom of impatience and a lack of tawakkul. The divine response underscores that true khushu' requires the worshipper to feel that their needs are being fulfilled in that very moment by God, rather than rushing to seek them elsewhere. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the inner dimension of prayer, where haste is interpreted as a subtle form of shirk in agency, attributing the speed of provision to causes other than Divine Will.
